---
title: 'Writing these docs'
description: 'How to add or change a documentation page: where files live, frontmatter and meta.json, the components and the style rules.'
---

These docs are plain MDX files in the repository, so they are reviewed and versioned like code. The web app serves them at `/docs` with [Fumadocs](https://fumadocs.dev), in the same Notebook layout as the mcoli-ui docs, with search. This page explains how to add or change one.

## Where pages live

Pages are MDX files in `apps/web/src/content/docs`, grouped in folders by section. The file path decides the address: `src/content/docs/build/contributing.mdx` is served at `/docs/build/contributing`, and an `index.mdx` is served at its folder's address (`src/content/docs/index.mdx` is `/docs`).

Each folder has a `meta.json` that names the section and orders the sidebar. Its `pages` list holds the file names without `.mdx` and the names of subfolders:

```json
{
  "title": "Build MCID",
  "description": "For people who work on MCID itself: how to contribute and how these docs are written.",
  "pages": ["architecture", "local-setup", "api-guide"]
}
```

The folder titles and descriptions also make the cards of the docs home. The `api-reference` folder is generated, its `meta.json` files included: change the generator in `apps/web/src/features/docs/api-reference`, never the files.

## Add a page

<Steps>

1. Create the file in the right folder, for example `src/content/docs/build/my-page.mdx`.

2. Start it with frontmatter that gives a `title` and a `description` of 30 to 160 characters. The title becomes the page heading and the browser title, and the description is shown under it and is its search snippet. Write each value as a quoted string, as Prettier formats it.

3. Add the file name, without `.mdx`, to the `pages` list of the folder's `meta.json`, where it belongs in the sidebar.

4. Write the content. Do not add a title heading, because the page already shows the title from the frontmatter. Start with a short introduction and then use `##` sections.

5. Run the docs tests, which check that every page is in a `meta.json`, that every link and anchor resolves, and that the page is valid MDX.

</Steps>

```mdx
---
title: 'My page'
description: 'What this page explains, in one sentence that reads well as a search result.'
---

A short introduction.

## A section
```

```bash
pnpm --filter @mcid/web exec vitest run tests/features/docs
```

## Components

Fenced code blocks get syntax highlighting (Shiki) and a copy button automatically. Always name the language after the opening fence. Headings get an anchor link and appear in the table of contents on the right.

A `Callout` draws attention to something. It has a `type` of `note`, `tip` or `warning`:

```mdx
<Callout type="warning">
  The end to end tests clear every table.
</Callout>
```

<Callout type="note">
  This is what a note looks like. The icon and the label carry the meaning, so it does not depend on colour.
</Callout>

`Steps` turns a numbered list into a procedure, as in "Add a page" above. Leave a blank line after the opening tag and before the closing tag.

`Tabs` offers alternatives, for example one example in several languages. They are the Fumadocs tabs:

```mdx
<Tabs defaultValue="node">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="node">Node</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="python">Python</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="node">Node example here.</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="python">Python example here.</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

`Diagram` shows an SVG with required alternative text. Put the file in `apps/web/public/docs/`:

```mdx
<Diagram src="/docs/system-overview.svg" alt="Projects call the API, which reads PostgreSQL." width={960} height={540} />
```

Tables scroll sideways inside their own box on narrow screens, so wide tables are fine.

The reference pages also use `Endpoint` (a method and a path), `SwaggerLink` (an operation in Swagger) and `InboundContract` (a table read from `@mcid/contracts`). Every component a page can use is listed in `apps/web/src/features/docs/mdx.tsx`.

## How it is built

`apps/web/source.config.ts` declares the collection and its frontmatter schema. The `fumadocs-mdx` plugin in `next.config.ts` compiles it and writes its index to `apps/web/.source/` (ignored by git) whenever `next dev` or `next build` starts, so there is no extra command. `src/features/docs/source.ts` turns it into the page tree, and `src/app/docs` holds the layout, the page route and its metadata. Search is served by `src/app/api/search/route.ts`. The brand styling is in `src/features/docs/docs.css`.

## Style rules

- Use plain hyphens. Do not use em dashes or en dashes in prose. A code block that quotes real program output keeps the output exactly as it was.
- Write in the present tense, and say what the code does, not what it was meant to do.
- Run every command and example you include.
- End each page with a line that starts with `Source:` and names the files it describes, so a reviewer can check a claim against the code.
- Link to other pages with absolute paths such as `/docs/build/contributing`, and to headings with `#anchors`.
- Keep the description short enough to read as a search result.

## What the tests check

The tests in `apps/web/tests/features/docs` build the page tree from the files with the Fumadocs loader. They fail when a `meta.json` lists a page that has no file, when a page is missing from its folder's `meta.json`, when a page has no title or description, when a page is not valid MDX, when it contains a top-level heading, when a code block does not name its language, when its prose uses an em or en dash (a code block may quote program output exactly), when it does not end with a `Source:` line, or when an internal link or anchor does not resolve.

Source: `apps/web/source.config.ts`, `apps/web/src/features/docs/source.ts`, `apps/web/src/features/docs/mdx.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/docs`, `apps/web/tests/features/docs`.
